article.title: Why a Two-Minute Check Can Prevent a Long Rework
article.why: 用短時間的針對性檢查降低返工成本。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A two-minute check can feel unnecessary when you have already finished a task. You may want to send the file, close the laptop, and move on. However, a very short check can prevent a much longer rework later.

The key is not to check everything again. Instead, check the few places where mistakes are most likely or most expensive. Before sending a spreadsheet, confirm the date range, filters, units, and file name. Before sending an email, check the recipient, attachment, and main request. Before submitting code, confirm that the final version runs with the expected input.

This works because many errors are small but costly. A missing filter may take only one second to fix before delivery. After delivery, the same mistake may require a new analysis, another review, an explanation to the client, and a corrected file. The correction itself is easy; the surrounding work is expensive.

A short check also helps when you are tired or moving quickly. People often make simple mistakes when they switch between tasks. A fixed checklist reduces the need to remember every risk at the last moment.

The checklist should stay short. If it becomes twenty items long, you may stop using it. Choose three to five checks based on errors that have happened before or errors that would cause serious problems. Different tasks can have different lists.

You can also improve the checklist over time. When a mistake happens, ask whether one simple check could have caught it. If yes, add that check or replace a less useful one. In this way, the list becomes a small record of practical experience.

The goal is not perfect work with zero mistakes. The goal is to spend a tiny amount of time where it has high value. Two minutes before delivery can be much cheaper than thirty minutes of rework after delivery. Before you press Send today, check the few things that would be most annoying to fix later.
paragraphs.zh: 完成任務後不必全部重做一次檢查，而是花兩分鐘確認最常出錯或出錯代價最高的項目。短 checklist 能把事前一秒可修正的小錯，擋在需要重新分析、重新審核與重新說明之前。
paragraphs.ja: 作業完了後に全項目を再確認するのではなく、ミスが起きやすい箇所や影響の大きい箇所だけを短時間で確認すると、後工程の大きな手戻りを防ぎやすくなります。

business.explanation: 用返工成本決定檢查重點

quiz.question: Why should a final checklist stay short?
quiz.answer: A short list is easier to use consistently and can focus on the highest-risk errors.
